```markdown
# Spec: Note pinning
Spec ID: SPEC-01
Status: draft
Supersedes: —

## Problem & user
Users of the notes API accumulate many notes, and the ones they need most often are buried in the `GET /notes` list. They have no way to keep important notes at the top. This costs them scrolling and searching on every read.

## Goals / Non-goals
Goals:
- A user can keep up to 3 chosen notes at the top of their note list.

Non-goals:
- Ordering among pinned notes beyond a stated rule is not redesigned here.
- Pinning notes shared with or owned by other users.
- Folders, tags or other organisation features.

## User stories
- US-1: As a note owner, I want to pin a note, so that it appears first in my list.
- US-2: As a note owner, I want to unpin a note, so that it returns to normal ordering and frees a pin slot.

## Acceptance criteria (EARS)
### API
- [ ] AC-1 WHEN the owner pins an unpinned note and fewer than 3 of their notes are pinned, the notes API shall mark the note as pinned and return a success response. [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: route and method for pin/unpin (e.g. a PATCH on the note or dedicated pin routes) — OQ-1]
- [ ] AC-2 IF the owner pins a note while 3 of their notes are already pinned, THEN the notes API shall reject the request, leave all pins unchanged, and return [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: status code and error body for the limit being exceeded — OQ-2].
- [ ] AC-3 WHEN the owner pins a note that is already pinned, the notes API shall leave the pin state unchanged and return [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: success or conflict response for re-pinning — OQ-3].
- [ ] AC-4 WHEN the owner unpins a pinned note, the notes API shall mark the note as not pinned so that the owner's pinned count decreases by 1.
- [ ] AC-5 IF a pin or unpin request names a note that does not exist or belongs to another user, THEN the notes API shall change no note and return [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: 404 for both cases, or 403 for another user's note — OQ-4].
- [ ] AC-6 WHEN `GET /notes` is called, the notes API shall return the caller's pinned notes before all unpinned notes.
- [ ] AC-7 WHEN `GET /notes` is called, the notes API shall order the pinned notes among themselves by [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: pin time, creation time, or last update — OQ-5].
- [ ] AC-8 WHEN `GET /notes` is called, the notes API shall order unpinned notes as it does today [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: current default order is not defined in the code read — OQ-6].
- [ ] AC-9 The `GET /notes` response shall include, for each note, whether it is pinned.
- [ ] AC-10 WHEN a pinned note is deleted via `DELETE /notes/:id`, the notes API shall stop counting it toward the owner's limit of 3.

## Edge cases
- Two concurrent pin requests when 2 notes are pinned: at most 3 notes end up pinned (AC-2).
- A user with no notes or no pinned notes: `GET /notes` returns the normal list (AC-6).
- Pin limit is per user, not global (AC-1, AC-2).

## Non-functional requirements
- NFR-1: The pin limit of 3 shall be enforced on the server, regardless of client behaviour.
- NFR-2: `GET /notes` p95 latency shall not increase by more than [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: budget in ms — OQ-7] relative to before the feature.

## Inputs and provenance
Data inputs:

| Input | Source | Trusted? | Freshness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Note id in pin/unpin request | API caller | No | Per request |
| Caller identity | Existing request authentication (not read in this run) | Assumed yes | Per request |
| Stored notes and pin state | Database/store | Yes | Current |

Requirement provenance:
- Pin limit of 3 and pinned-first ordering: the request.
- Existing routes `GET /notes`, `POST /notes`, `DELETE /notes/:id`: `src/notes/routes.ts:2-4`.
- Specs normally live in `docs/specs/`: `AGENTS.md:3`. This spec was saved elsewhere at the caller's explicit instruction.

## Untrusted inputs
| Input | Threat | Covered by |
|---|---|---|
| Note id in pin/unpin request | Pinning another user's or a nonexistent note | AC-5 |
| Note id in pin/unpin request | Exceeding the pin limit by repeated or concurrent requests | AC-2, NFR-1 |

## Open questions
- OQ-1: What route and method pin and unpin a note? — default if unanswered: `POST /notes/:id/pin` and `DELETE /notes/:id/pin` — blocks: AC-1
- OQ-2: What response is returned when the limit is exceeded? — default if unanswered: 409 with an error message naming the limit of 3 — blocks: AC-2
- OQ-3: What is returned when pinning an already pinned note? — default if unanswered: 200, idempotent no-op — blocks: AC-3
- OQ-4: Status for missing versus another user's note? — default if unanswered: 404 for both — blocks: AC-5
- OQ-5: How are pinned notes ordered among themselves? — default if unanswered: most recently pinned first — blocks: AC-7
- OQ-6: What is the current order of unpinned notes? — default if unanswered: preserve whatever order exists today — blocks: AC-8
- OQ-7: Latency budget for `GET /notes`? — default if unanswered: +20 ms at p95 — blocks: NFR-2

## Changelog
- 2026-10-21 · draft — created — new feature spec
```

Spec ID: SPEC-01
Status: draft
Supersedes: —

## Problem & user
Users of the notes API keep personal notes that only the creating user can see. An owner who wants another person to see a note has no way to do so within the product. This feature lets an owner share a note with another user, identified by that user's email address.

## Goals / Non-goals
Goals
- An owner can give another user access to one of the owner's notes by entering that user's email address.

Non-goals
- None recorded; the request names no exclusions. Revoking a share, notifying the recipient and sharing with groups are not requested and are not specified here (see report notes to the caller).

## User stories
- US-1: As a note owner, I want to share a note with another user by entering their email address, so that the other user can access the note.
- US-2: As a recipient, I want to see notes shared with me, so that I can use them. (Derived from the share goal; the request does not state how the recipient finds shared notes. See OQ-4.)

## Acceptance criteria (EARS)
### API
- [ ] AC-1 WHEN an owner submits a share request for a note the owner owns, with the email address of a registered user, the notes API shall record a share of that note for that user.
- [ ] AC-2 IF a user who does not own a note submits a share request for it, THEN the notes API shall reject the request and record no share.
- [ ] AC-3 IF the share request names a note that does not exist, THEN the notes API shall reject the request and record no share.
- [ ] AC-4 IF the email address in a share request does not belong to a registered user, THEN the notes API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: reject the request, or hold a pending share until that email registers? — OQ-3].
- [ ] AC-5 WHEN a share exists, the recipient shall be permitted to [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: read only, or read and edit the shared note? — OQ-1].
- [ ] AC-6 WHEN an owner deletes a note that has one or more shares, the notes API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: remove the shares along with the note, keep the note for recipients, or block the deletion? — OQ-2].

## Edge cases
- The owner shares a note with the same email address twice: expected behaviour not decided (see report notes); not covered by an AC.
- The owner enters their own email address: expected behaviour not decided; not covered by an AC.
- The email address is malformed: not decided; the validation rule is not covered by an AC.
- The owner deletes a shared note: see AC-6.
- The email address belongs to no registered user: see AC-4.

## Non-functional requirements
- NFR-1: The notes API shall respond to a share request within 500 ms at p95. (Proposed value; not given in the request.)
- NFR-2: The notes API shall log each created share with the note identifier, owner identifier and recipient identifier, and shall not log the full recipient email address.

Data inputs

|---|---|---|---|

# Spec: Note sharing
Spec ID: SPEC-01
Status: draft
Supersedes: —

## Problem & user
Users of the notes API keep personal notes that only the owner can see. To let another person see a note, the owner has no way to do it inside the product. This spec lets an owner share a note with another user, identified by the recipient's email address.

## Goals / Non-goals
Goals:
- An owner can share one of their notes with another user by email.
- A recipient can find the notes shared with them.
- An owner stays in control of who a note is shared with.

Non-goals:
- Sharing with groups, teams or public links.
- Sharing by any identifier other than email.
- Real-time collaboration or conflict resolution between editors.

## User stories
- US-1: As a note owner, I want to share a note with another user by email, so that they can access it.
- US-2: As a recipient, I want to see the notes shared with me, so that I can open them.
- US-3: As a note owner, I want to see and stop a share, so that I control who has access.

## Acceptance criteria (EARS)

### API
- [ ] AC-1 WHEN an authenticated owner submits a share request for a note they own with a well-formed email address, the notes API shall record a share of that note for that email.
- [ ] AC-2 IF the caller is not the owner of the note, THEN the notes API shall reject the share request and record no share.
- [ ] AC-3 IF the note does not exist, THEN the notes API shall reject the share request with a not-found error.
- [ ] AC-4 IF the submitted email address is not well-formed, THEN the notes API shall reject the request and record no share.
- [ ] AC-5 WHEN a recipient lists their notes, the notes API shall include the notes shared with them, marked as shared and distinguishable from notes they own.
- [ ] AC-6 WHEN a recipient opens a note shared with them, the notes API shall return the note content.
- [ ] AC-7 WHERE the recipient is granted a permission level, the notes API shall allow the recipient to [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: read only, or read and edit? — OQ-1].
- [ ] AC-8 WHEN the owner deletes a note that has shares, the notes API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: remove the shares with the note, keep the note for recipients, or reject the deletion? — OQ-2].
- [ ] AC-9 WHEN an owner shares a note with an email address that has no account, the notes API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: reject, hold a pending share until sign-up, or send an invitation? — OQ-3].
- [ ] AC-10 WHEN an owner stops sharing a note with an email address, the notes API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: is revoking a share in scope, and through which request? — OQ-4].
- [ ] AC-11 WHEN an owner shares a note with an email address it is already shared with, the notes API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: treat as success without a duplicate, or return an error? — OQ-5].
- [ ] AC-12 IF an owner shares a note with their own email address, THEN the notes API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: reject or ignore? — OQ-6].
- [ ] AC-13 IF a user who is neither the owner nor a recipient requests a note, THEN the notes API shall deny access exactly as it does for any note that is not theirs.

## Edge cases
- Email letter case differs between share and account: the outcome is [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: is email matching case-insensitive? — OQ-7].
- A recipient changes their account email after a share: the outcome is [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: does the share follow the account or the address? — OQ-8].
